standard_prerequisites.name: Skew product over an interval exchange transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: The extension T_f acts on the product of the interval with the torus by combining the base transformation with the cocycle f, and its ergodicity is measured with respect to the product of the invariant measures.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the transformation whose ergodicity is concluded.

standard_prerequisites.name: Rokhlin towers with prescribed displacement
standard_prerequisites.statement: There are subsets that decompose into towers of bounded height, of small base and with uniformly small displacement over the tower height.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are required by the second condition of the statement and are what makes the criterion effective.

standard_prerequisites.name: Essential values
standard_prerequisites.statement: The essential values of the cocycle form a closed subgroup of the range, and ergodicity of the skew product is equivalent to that subgroup being the whole space.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion that the effective conditions are designed to reach.

core_obligations: Under the four stated conditions on the cocycle — differentiability on the exchanged intervals, existence of towers with the prescribed bounds, the interval spanned by each point and its return lying in a continuity interval, and the two-sided derivative bounds — verify the hypotheses of the criterion of Conze and Fraczek, using the towers to satisfy its first three numbered conditions (source lines 1084-1162).
Show that the fourth numbered condition of that criterion, the uniform bound on the Birkhoff sums along the tower, is exactly the first half of the fourth stated condition (source lines 1084-1162).

Conclude that the average of the cocycle lies in the group of essential values, and then use the ergodicity of the product of the base transformation with itself to obtain ergodicity of the extension (source lines 1084-1162).

proof_roadmap.step: Match the stated tower conditions with the numbered conditions of the Conze-Fraczek criterion.
Identify the Birkhoff-sum bound and locate the average in the group of essential values.
Apply the ergodicity of the product of the base transformation with itself to conclude.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 1065-1082: if the cocycle is differentiable on the exchanged intervals, if there are Rokhlin towers of bounded height, small base and uniformly small displacement, if the interval spanned by a point and its return lies in a continuity interval, and if the Birkhoff sums of the cocycle and of its derivative obey the stated two-sided bounds, then ergodicity of the product of the base transformation with itself implies ergodicity of the extension. The proof (source lines 1084-1162) is long and its whole content is a translation: each of the four stated conditions has to be matched with the corresponding hypothesis of the Conze-Fraczek criterion, the tower bounds have to be shown to imply its first three numbered conditions, and the Birkhoff-sum bound has to imply its fourth, after which the average of the cocycle is placed in the group of essential values. The statement records the conditions and the conclusion but none of the matching.
